info: In Portuguese, the simple past is formed by changing the ending of the verb to show who performed the action. The ending identifies the person and number of the subject, so the subject pronoun can often be omitted. For example, corri means “I ran,” with the -i ending identifying the first-person singular past. The exact endings depend partly on whether the verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir, and many common verbs have irregular forms.
